title: Detection of prescribed cohomological and Tor intervals by an exact tensor-compatible product decomposition
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ and $(\mathcal C_i,R_i)$, $i\in I$, be ringed sites, each small relative to the universe of module sheaves, with commutative ring sheaves; $I$ is a finite set, possibly empty. Write $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and $\mathcal M_i=\operatorname{Mod}(R_i)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and use their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], cohomology sheaves $H^m$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] and K-flat derived tensors $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent].

Suppose $r=(r_i)_i:\mathcal M\simeq\prod_i\mathcal M_i$ is an additive exact equivalence with additive exact quasi-inverse $G$. Define $e_iN=G((N_j)_j)$ for the tuple with $N_i=N$ and $N_j=0$ for $j\ne i$; the unit and counit identify $r_ie_iN\cong N$ and $r_je_iN\cong0$ for $j\ne i$. Let $D_i:D(\mathcal M)\to D(\mathcal M_i)$ be the functor induced by degreewise $r_i$. Assume natural comparisons
$$H^m(D_iK)\cong r_iH^m(K),\qquad D_i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\cong D_iK\otimes_{R_i}^{\mathbf L}D_iL$$
for all integers $m$ and all $K,L\in D(\mathcal M)$.

For any $K\in D(\mathcal M)$ and integers $a\le b$, one has
$$\bigl(H^m(K)=0\text{ for }m\notin[a,b]\bigr)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\forall i,\ H^m(D_iK)=0\text{ for }m\notin[a,b].$$
Define Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ in each category to mean $H^m(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}M[0])=0$ for every module sheaf $M$ and every $m\notin[a,b]$, where $M[0]$ denotes the complex concentrated in degree zero. Then
$$K\text{ has Tor amplitude in }[a,b]\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\forall i,\ D_iK\text{ has Tor amplitude in }[a,b].$$
The quantifiers in the right-hand condition include every $R_i$-module sheaf $N$: its global degree-zero test object is $(e_iN)[0]$, and the comparison identifies $D_i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(e_iN)[0])\cong D_iK\otimes_{R_i}^{\mathbf L}N[0]$. No boundedness or constructibility assumption on $K$ is imposed. The statements hold for $I=\varnothing$ whenever the displayed equivalence exists, and the zero object satisfies both interval conditions for every $a\le b$.

proof.text: A module M is zero if and only if all coordinate restrictions are zero. The forward implication follows because the additive coordinate functors preserve zero objects. Conversely, a tuple of zero objects is a zero object in the product category: maps to and from any tuple are the unique coordinatewise maps. The fully faithful equivalence reflects zero objects. This proof also covers the empty product, since equality of empty tuples is automatic.

proof.text: For every integer $m$, apply step 1 to $A=H^m(K)$ and the assumed isomorphisms $H^m(D_iK)\cong r_iH^m(K)$. Thus $H^m(K)=0$ if and only if all $H^m(D_iK)=0$. Quantifying over $m\notin[a,b]$ proves the cohomological equivalence. Here cohomology is a functor on the derived category, so it carries isomorphisms to isomorphisms.

proof.text: Use Mathlib CategoryTheory.Functor.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor at degree zero to identify D_i(M[0]) with (r_i M)[0]. The counit of the given product equivalence evaluated on the zero-insertion tuple gives r_i(e_i N) isomorphic to N, and r_j(e_i N) isomorphic to zero when j differs from i. Evaluate the assumed natural tensor comparison on (K,M[0]) and map the degree-zero comparison through the tensor bifunctor. For M=e_i N, compose with the image of the counit isomorphism under the single and tensor functors. This gives the required component tensor-test comparison.

proof.text: If $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, fix $i$, any $R_i$-module sheaf $N$, and $m\notin[a,b]$. Use the global module test $M=e_iN$. The global hypothesis gives $H^m(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(e_iN)[0])=0$. The assumed cohomology comparison, additivity of $r_i$ and step 3 give $H^m(D_iK\otimes_{R_i}^{\mathbf L}N[0])=0$. Since $N$ and $m$ were arbitrary, $D_iK$ has the prescribed Tor amplitude.

proof.text: Conversely suppose each $D_iK$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Fix any global module sheaf $M$ and $m\notin[a,b]$. The tensor comparison and step 3 identify $D_i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M[0])$ with $D_iK\otimes_{R_i}^{\mathbf L}(r_iM)[0]$, whose $m$-th cohomology is zero by the component hypothesis. Apply step 2 to the object $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M[0]$: its $m$-th cohomology is zero. Quantifying over all $M$ and $m$ proves the reverse Tor implication. No bound on $K$ was used.

proof.text: The tuple argument and all quantified equivalences already include the empty index set; no choice of an index occurs. For a zero derived object K, each cohomology functor preserves zero objects by additivity. For every module M, apply the separate additivity of the fixed published derived tensor from [lem-pur-derived-tensor-additive-constraints] with the second variable M[0]. That functor preserves zero objects, so K tensor^L M[0] is zero and its cohomology in every integer degree is zero. This proves every ordered interval assertion, without constructing a new resolution.
